events.title: Death of William Shakespeare
events.description: English playwright and poet William Shakespeare died in Stratford-upon-Avon. By tradition his birth is also celebrated on this date, though only his baptism on April 26, 1564 is documented. He died on the same date that Miguel de Cervantes was buried, though the two deaths fell on different calendar systems.
events.significance: Shakespeare is widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language, and his plays and sonnets continue to shape world literature and theater. UNESCO's World Book and Copyright Day is observed on April 23 in tribute to him and other authors.

events.title: Battle of Clontarf
events.description: Irish forces led by High King Brian Boru fought a coalition of Leinster rebels, Dublin Vikings, and Norse allies near Dublin. Brian's army won the battle, but Brian himself was killed in his tent after the fighting.
events.significance: The battle ended Viking power as a political force in Ireland and became a defining event in Irish historical memory, though Brian's death led to political fragmentation.

events.title: Founding of the Order of the Garter
events.description: King Edward III of England established the Order of the Garter, the senior and oldest surviving order of chivalry in England, around St George's Day.
events.significance: The Order remains the highest order of chivalry in the United Kingdom and reinforced the connection between monarchy, chivalric culture, and the cult of St George.

events.title: Coca-Cola Introduces New Coke
events.description: The Coca-Cola Company announced it was changing the formula of its flagship soft drink and launched 'New Coke'. Consumer backlash was swift and intense, and the original formula returned as 'Coca-Cola Classic' just 79 days later.
events.significance: The episode became a landmark case study in marketing and brand loyalty, showing the emotional attachment consumers can have to established products.

events.title: First YouTube Video Uploaded
events.description: Co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded 'Me at the zoo', an 18-second clip filmed at the San Diego Zoo, as the first video on YouTube.
events.significance: It marked the start of a platform that transformed media, entertainment, advertising, and communication by making online video sharing accessible to billions of people.
